Description

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling-basis.

FDA Office and Location: A research opportunity is available within the Office of Translational Sciences (OTS) Office of Clinical Pharmacology (OCP) Division of Applied Regulatory Science (DARS) at the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER) of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) located in Silver Spring, Maryland.

The Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER) performs an essential public health task by making sure that safe and effective drugs are available to improve the health of people in the United States. As part of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), CDER regulates over-the-counter and prescription drugs, including biological therapeutics and generic drugs. These efforts cover more than just medicines.

Research Project: The Food and Drug Administration is seeking a fellow for a Bioinformatics/Biostatistics research project in the Division of Applied Regulatory Science (DARS) located in the Office of Clinical Pharmacology (OCP), Office of Translational Sciences (OTS), Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER). DARS seeks to move new science into the regulatory review process and close the gap between scientific innovation and medical product review.

Biomarker research has been revolutionized by the availability of technologies for assaying biological activity on a global basis by measuring features of the genome, transcriptome, and proteome (so-called "omics"). Large-scale proteomics data has the potential to identify clinically meaningful biomarkers for predicting disease progression, monitoring treatment efficacy, and stratifying patients in clinical trials. DARS is actively evaluating innovative omics technologies and analytical approaches to develop biomarkers that can serve as qualified regulatory tools, supporting standardized endpoints for drug development and informed regulatory decision-making.

This fellowship represents an excellent learning opportunity to research in a visible program area with the potential to substantively advance omics-based biomarker discovery and drug development. You will be directly involved in the statistical analysis of large-scale omics data to inform biomarker discovery for disease expression and severity and to support the development of biomarkers relevant to disease progression and therapeutic response.

You will contribute to the study design and statistical analysis of large-scale omics data generated from biospecimens from clinical trials or well-characterized cohorts. The fellowship will utilize differential expression analysis, systems-level analysis to identify molecular composites and organ-specific signatures, and correlation analyses between molecular markers and disease severity or treatment response. This will include quality control of omics data, statistical modeling, multivariate analysis, pathway and network analysis, data visualization, literature review, and manuscript preparation.

Learning Objectives

Learn to perform quality control and preprocessing of large-scale datasets relevant to regulatory biomarker development.Learn to design and conduct statistical analyses supporting biomarker discovery, including differential expression analysis, effect size estimation, and correction for multiple comparisons.Learn to apply advanced statistical and machine learning methods for identifying multi-protein biomarker panels and assess their correlation with clinical outcomes.Learn to conduct systems-level analyses to identify protein composites, organ-specific signatures, and potential pathways or networks associated with disease phenotypes or drug response.Learn to analyze and interpret omics data within the regulatory science framework to inform drug development and regulatory review.Learn to conduct literature reviews and prepare scientific manuscripts supporting regulatory research dissemination and potential biomarker qualification.

Mentor: The mentor for this opportunity is Paula Hyland (Paula.Hyland@fda.hhs.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research, please contact the mentor.

Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens, Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR), and foreign nationals. Non-U.S. citizen applicants should refer to the Guidelines for Non-U.S. Citizens Details page of the program website for information about the valid immigration statuses that are acceptable for program participation.

This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education, was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and FDA. The participant will receive a monthly stipend commensurate with educational level and experience. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Participants do not become employees of FDA, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits.

Completion of a successful background investigation by the Office of Personnel Management is required for an applicant to be on-boarded at FDA. OPM can complete a background investigation only for individuals, including non-US Citizens, who have resided in the US for a total of three of the past five years.

Qualifications

The qualified candidate should be currently pursuing or have received a doctoral degree in one of the relevant fields (e.g. molecular biology, cell biology, genetics or genomics, biomedical sciences, pharmaceutical sciences, bioinformatics, biostatistics, or a closely related discipline.).

Preferred Skills

Background in statistical analysis methods including differential expression analysis, multivariate statistics, and correction for multiple comparisons (e.g., Bonferroni, Benjamini-Hochberg, FDR).Experience with analysis of one or more omics data types (e.g., proteomics, genomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics, or epigenomics) and large-scale biological datasets.Working knowledge of statistical programming languages (R, Python) and data visualization tools.Familiarity with pathway analysis methods.Experience with quality control procedures for high-throughput biological data.Knowledge of data mining approaches for biomarker discovery, with the ability to interpret findings in a biological context.Excellent teamwork, organizational, communication, and time-management skills.Ability to multitask, prioritize efficiently, and work independently as well as part of a collaborative team.

The insights the Analyst will deliver will originate from both cadenced and ad-hoc research requests, while the feedback the Senior Analyst gathers will inform how we optimize & evolve the Digital & Social Intelligence capability over time using ever-evolving AI-driven technology.

The Senior Analyst will be expected to balance supporting stakeholders by fulfilling research requests using our best-in-class technology stack, while also training the stakeholders to be able to leverage the technology to find insights on their own. This balance will allow the Senior Analyst, along with the rest of the Digital & Social Intelligence team, to focus our efforts on the most important in-depth analysis the organization needs, while empowering our stakeholders to conduct their own light monitoring of day-to-day digital & social insights questions. The role will work in collaboration with other stakeholders within the Center of Demand Generation, including but not limited to Foresight, Consumer Insights, Digital Analytics, Marketing Analytics, Digital Shelf & eCommerce, Shopper Insights and Innovation, to provide capabilities and services that consistently identify, generate & distribute actionable & timely insights to Nestle USA’s 25+ Brand Marketing teams.

The Senior Analyst will be expected to work with our stakeholder teams to understand Nestle USA’s business objectives and brand strategies across a wide variety of product categories such as coffee, coffee creamer, chocolate & desserts, frozen meals, pizza, snacking, baking ingredients, noodles and sauces. Day-to-day activities vary given the nature of our business, but the Senior Analyst can expect to balance answering business questions through in-depth analysis using multiple technologies, collaborating with stakeholders in key meetings, developing and executing self-service training programs, identifying & helping implement new technology features, working with vendors and attending leadership presentations.

On top of the various product categories we support and the multiple technologies we use, the world of social media and AI-driven technology changes rapidly. Therefore, a balance of technical skill, strategic thinking, proactivity, flexibility and a solution-seeking attitude is crucial for success in this role.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Social Listening, LLM Listening & Related Social Media Research, including Presentation to Stakeholders. Leverage Nestle USA’s Digital & Social Intelligence technology stack to conduct in-depth research about our brands, competitors, product categories and relevant cultural trends, using the insights to deliver a persuasive & visual story to stakeholders that drives action within their key initiatives. This includes navigating technology that handles every facet of Digital & Social Intelligence, such as social listening, ratings & reviews listening, LLM Listening / GEO / AEO, emerging trend identification, social audience persona building, influencer evaluation and owned content performance benchmarking. Where applicable, this also includes combining findings with other data sources outside of Social Intelligence, often via collaboration with our broader Digital Analytics, Marketing Analytics and Consumer Insights teams, to provide comprehensive analysis to the stakeholder. Stakeholder Training & Guidance. Assist in the development and execution of training programs, including building training material, leading office hours and sitting one-on-one with stakeholders to guide them through use cases for social listening & social intelligence that build confidence in their ability to navigate the technology to find insights.Stakeholder Request Management. Assist the Digital & Social Intelligence Manager in managing an analysis request queue, which assigns priority to each ad-hoc social research request based on impact to the business, level of effort and urgency. This includes keeping track of stakeholder check-in cadences to ensure the Digital & Social Intelligence team is consistently engaging each key stakeholder group. Tool Output Scanning & Insights Identification. Review the automated reporting outputs from the various tools, including weekly/bi-weekly/monthly AI-driven reports and real-time email alerts, to ensure continuous improvement in the quality of the automated outputs while also mining for actionable insights that need to be flagged to our stakeholders for further discussion & potential action.Tool Maintenance & Governance. Assist in the day-to-day management of the tools, from user access to dashboard/report quality, flagging issues or needs to the Digital & Social Intelligence Manager while collaborating with 3rd party and shared service support teams. Vendor Collaboration. Partnering with analysts from 3rd parties and shared service teams on key research projects and key feature advancements, as well as brainstorming and providing feedback to tool providers on ideal features and functionality that maximize actionability. 
REQUIREMENTS AND MINIMUM EDUCATION LEVEL:

Bachelor's degree in marketing, market research, analytics, communications, business, economics, or related field3-5 years of experience in social listening and additional social research, including in-tool navigational experience and strategic storytelling of analysis results.3-5 years in a strategic role working with data analytics, with a focus on developing strong dashboards and/or other automatically refreshable visualizations that empower stakeholders to quickly identify key takeaways from data
DESIRED EXPERIENCE:

-

rows.title: Insurance Public Policy Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Company Overview

KKR is a leading global investment firm that offers alternative asset management as well as capital markets and insurance solutions. KKR aims to generate attractive investment returns by following a patient and disciplined investment approach, employing world-class people, and supporting growth in its portfolio companies and communities. KKR sponsors investment funds that invest in private equity, credit and real assets and has strategic partners that manage hedge funds. KKR’s insurance subsidiaries offer retirement, life and reinsurance products under the management of Global Atlantic Financial Group. References to KKR’s investments may include the activities of its sponsored funds and insurance subsidiaries.

Team Overview

Established in 2008, the Public Policy & Affairs team works in partnership with the KKR Global Institute (KGI), KKR leadership, industry and country teams, portfolio companies, limited partners and other stakeholders to facilitate better investing through a better understanding of the intersection between policy and politics. The team helps guide KKR’s investments and portfolio companies on legislative, regulatory, and reputational considerations to help manage risks and identify opportunities. The team collaborates with our Legal, Compliance, Investment, Risk, Finance, Technology, and other teams to manage and protect the firm’s license to operate.

Position Summary

The KKR Public Policy team seeks to hire an Analyst based in Washington, D.C. who will be fully dedicated to supporting Global Atlantic Financial Group, KKR’s life insurance and reinsurance business. The position will report to the Managing Director, Regulatory & Government Affairs, Insurance. The individual will monitor and analyze insurance regulatory and public policy developments, help the team to assess their potential implications for Global Atlantic, and translate complex issues into actionable intelligence for senior executives and business leaders. The Analyst will work closely with Global Atlantic leadership, including senior legal and regulatory stakeholders, and will support engagement with regulators, policymakers, trade associations, and other external stakeholders. The role requires strong judgment, analytical and communication skills, and the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, highly commercial environment. This is an in-office position and requires working from KKR’s Washington, D.C. office five days per week.

Responsibilities

Insurance Regulatory and Legislative Monitoring and Analysis: Monitor, track, and analyze U.S. state insurance regulatory and legislative developments, including activity involving state insurance departments, the National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC), the National Organization of Life and Health Insurance Guaranty Associations (NOLHGA), and the National Council of Insurance Legislators (NCOIL). Assess emerging risks and opportunities for Global Atlantic and provide timely, targeted updates to senior executives and other internal stakeholders.Executive Communications and Presentations: Develop clear, concise, and polished presentations, briefing materials, regulatory updates, and other content for Global Atlantic and KKR senior executives and other senior stakeholders.Regulator and Policymaker Engagement: Prepare briefing notes, background materials, and related content for senior executives ahead of meetings with insurance regulators, policymakers, and other government officials, and support preparation and follow-up associated with those engagements.Regulatory Priorities and Cross-Functional Coordination: Partner closely with Legal, Compliance, KCS, Bermuda, Risk, and other business functions to coordinate engagement on key regulatory and policy issues, maintain internal regulatory-priorities materials and dashboards, and support consistent and effective reporting to senior leadership.Regulatory Reporting and Analysis: Develop internal reports and analyses that synthesize regulatory developments, identify emerging themes, and explain potential implications for Global Atlantic’s business, strategic priorities, and operating environment.Relevant Insurance Trades: Track discussions, initiatives, and emerging issues across relevant insurance trade associations; synthesize key developments; and provide targeted updates to appropriate internal subject-matter experts and senior stakeholders.International Insurance Policy: Monitor relevant international insurance supervisory and financial-policy developments, including work involving the International Association of Insurance Supervisors (IAIS), International Monetary Fund (IMF), Bank for International Settlements (BIS), Financial Stability Board (FSB), and other relevant institutions, and assess potential implications for U.S. insurance regulation and Global Atlantic.External Advisors and Consultants: Help manage and leverage external advisors and consultants to source timely policy and regulatory intelligence, deepen the team’s understanding of emerging issues, and support efforts to advance Global Atlantic’s positions on key regulatory and public policy priorities.Travel and External Engagement: Travel as needed to represent Global Atlantic at industry conferences and meetings with insurance regulators, policymakers, and other external stakeholders, and to support senior executives in connection with relevant external engagements. 

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree required.2+ years of meaningful private-sector experience is required, preferably, in public policy, government and/or regulatory affairs, insurance, or related industries.Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with demonstrated ability to develop high-quality materials for senior executives.Demonstrated ability to use AI-enabled tools thoughtfully to improve the consistency, quality, and efficiency of recurring workflows.Strong presentation capabilities and comfort communicating with senior internal and external stakeholders.Basic understanding of the U.S. state-based insurance regulatory system, including familiarity with the NAIC.Knowledge of the interplay among U.S. state and federal policymakers, and the ability to assess how developments across jurisdictions may affect Global Atlantic.General familiarity with the U.S. federal policy landscape and the legislative, regulatory, and political dynamics relevant to financial services and insurance.General understanding of international insurance supervisory dynamics and relevant institutions, including the IAIS, IMF, BIS, and FSB.Strong proficiency in PowerPoint, Word, and Excel.Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills – can develop trusted relationships with a variety of constituents, build credibility quickly, and partner effectively with others.Ability to prioritize among competing demands in a fast-paced environment.Excellent knowledge of Microsoft Office suite, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.

CRITICAL COMPENTENCIES FOR SUCCESS

Ability to quickly learn complex insurance, reinsurance, accounting, financial, capital, and regulatory concepts and translate them clearly for different audiences.Deep intellectual curiosity and a demonstrated instinct to understand how policy and regulatory developments affect the business.Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify relevant implications from complex or evolving issues.Exceptional written and oral communication and presentation skills, including the judgment and presence to communicate effectively with senior executives.Excellent judgment, maturity, discretion, and attention to detail.Strong project and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines simultaneously.High degree of ownership, initiative, and responsiveness, with the flexibility and team orientation to contribute across a broad range of execution-oriented responsibilities at every level in support of a lean team.Collaborative, low-ego team player who prioritizes team outcomes and builds productive relationships across legal, compliance, business, investment, and external stakeholder groups.Ability to operate effectively in a dynamic, fast-paced, highly commercial, and high-expectation environment.

This is the expected annual base salary range for this Washington DC-based position. Actual salaries may vary based on factors, such as skill, experience, and qualification for the role. Employees may be eligible for a discretionary bonus, based on factors such as individual and team performance.

$90,000—$120,000 USD

rows.title: Watchlist Analyst Junior
rows.descriptionText:
Purpose and Impact:

Amentum provides warning and all-source analytical support to DIA’s Defense Combating Terrorism Office to drive DoD policy, planning, and operational decisions to counter regional and transnational terrorism threats. We conduct mission-critical counterterrorism analysis focused on operational and strategic effects against emerging terrorist threat networks and identities operating globally with intent to harm U.S. persons, facilities, and interests. Our work includes delivering national watchlisting support to the TIDE database, providing expert assessments for the Pentagon/Joint Staff, and 24/7/365 support to DoD and senior policy decision makers, as well as international and interagency partners, on predictive threat assessments regarding transnational and regional terrorist threats. Amentum analysts also support the Congressionally-mandated Prisoner of War/Missing in Action cell with analysis, collection, and 24/7 support to the U.S. government for global hostage threats or events against U.S. citizens.

Work Schedule: First Shift – 8 hours per day

Essential Responsibilities:

Systematically and deliberately reviews DoD datasets assessed as likely to contain identifying information for known or suspected terrorists. Identity, prioritize, and record information from known DoD datasets related to known or suspected terrorists as specified by the Government. Crosscheck/research known or suspected terrorists against other intelligence holdings to ensure completeness of information and to avoid duplicating data entries. Compile information into a nomination report format as specified by the Government. Correctly format, classify, and address reports. Ensure information contained within reports is intelligible, cogent, comprehensive, and understandable, and that all reports use proper grammar and spelling. Meet Terrorist Identity Nomination (TIN) production schedule. Correct and resubmit incorrect reports and prepare reports for dissemination as record message traffic or other dissemination methods as specified by the Government. Provide guidance and instruction for less experienced team members assigned to Watchlisting. Demonstrate general knowledge and understanding of IC organizations associated with CT operations, analysis, products, and information systems. Attend and participate in meetings, conferences, intelligence exchanges, roundtables, working groups, and other types of analytic exchanges in support or DIA’s Watchlisting mission. Possess general information systems experience working with select DoD datasets and intelligence reporting activities: demonstrate comprehensive mission knowledge in order to provide guidance related to National Terrorist Watchlisting policies and procedures. Demonstrate in-depth knowledge and understanding of terrorist organizations, to include group names and geographic location, leadership, activities, and ideology. 

Minimum Requirements (Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities):

Watchlist Analyst – Performs all-source intelligence analysis of DoD datasets to identify and nominate known or suspected terrorists into the National Terrorist Watchlisting system. Develops DoD recommendations for the no-fly, selectee, or other national terrorist watch lists as appropriate, to fulfill the DoD component of Homeland Security Presidential Directives (HSPDs) 6 and 11 and reviews DoD datasets for identifying information of Known or Suspected Terrorists; and identifies, prioritizes, and records information from DoD datasets as specified by the Government. Produces analytic reports using DIA’s Watchlisting Data Organizer (WATCHDOG) and / or other internal DIA production tools. Prepares reports for dissemination by methods specified by the Government.

Clearance Required: 

TS/SCI w/Poly

Minimum Education: 

High School/GED

Minimum Years of Experience:

2 Years

Preferred Qualifications:

Desired Experience: 4 years of experience related to the specific labor category with at least a portion of the experience within the last 2 years. Desired Education: Bachelor’s degree in an area related to the labor category from a college or university accredited by an agency recognized by the U.S. Department of Education. Demonstrates understanding of the 200 Series of ODNI’s ICDs: 203 - Analytic Standards, 206 – Sourcing Requirements for Disseminated Products, and 208 - Write for Maximum Utility. Produce formal written strategic counterterrorism and or all source intelligence assessments, products, graphics and briefings in accordance with ICD 203, DIA and ODNI standards as appropriate. Demonstrates ability to use research databases (e.g., Global Terrorism Database) and use quantifiable matrices in a professional setting to prepare written and oral products on complex topics. 

As part of our commitment to maintaining a safe and compliant work environment, Amentum is a drug-free workplace and requires all personnel to comply with company drug and alcohol policies as a condition of employment. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of the drug screening process. Please note that this may include pre-hire screening for marijuana, as well as other federally controlled substances due to Amentum’s role as a federal contractor and trusted partner to the US Government. 

Other Responsibilities:

Safety - Amentum enforces a safety culture whereby all employees have the responsibility for continuously developing and maintaining a safe work environment. As appropriate, each employee is responsible for completing all training requirements and fulfilling all self-aid/buddy aid responsibilities, participating in emergency response tasks and serving on safety committees and teams.

Quality - Quality is the foundation for the management of our business and the keystone to our goal of customer satisfaction. It is our policy to consistently provide services that meet customer expectations. Accordingly, each employee must conform to the Amentum Quality Policy and carry out job activities in compliance with applicable Amentum Quality System documents and customer contracts. Each employee must read and understand his/her Quality Management and Customer Satisfaction responsibilities.

Procedure Compliance - Each employee must read, understand and implement the general and specific operational, safety, quality and environmental requirements of all plans, procedures and policies pertaining to his/her job.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status.

rows.title: Research Associate
rows.descriptionText:
At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future.

Department Summary:

The Market Intelligence and Research team

MITRE is seeking a curious and collaborative early career Research Analyst, Research Associate, Information Professional, or Librarian to join our Research Services team, a part of MITRE’s Market Intelligence & Research organization. This individual will be responsible for providing, locating, gathering, and analyzing information from third-parties, open-source news and articles, published research papers, subscription and public databases and other sources in support of MITRE’s work programs, and specific sponsor and MITRE initiatives.

As a research associate, this key team member will need a growing understanding and/or interest in databases, digital research libraries, query techniques and short cuts, research and information management practices, and OS intelligence platforms (news alerts, dashboards). This role focuses on desk research, secondary research, literature searching/review, open-source and subscription-based research, and synthesis of existing information for internal clients. This is not a primary research, laboratory, engineering, scientific, or product research role.

This role will translate internal client questions into tangible research objectives to meet the needs of our customers and will engage with internal clients to scope and prioritize tasks, collecting and working with a variety of research outputs, and performing additional desk and secondary research as necessary. This position supports other department capabilities in business analyses, strategy, and sponsor and market intelligence as needed. This role will interact with all levels of the company, including senior level managers, technical SMEs, and analysts.

The ideal candidate is intellectually curious, highly motivated to find answers, and eager to develop a consultative approach to research support by helping clients refine questions, identify the most relevant sources, and shape actionable outputs. The ideal candidate will have interest in performing research on a broad range of topics, an entrepreneurial approach to generating and creating value and impact, and an appreciation for a nonprofit/public interest environment.

Research Analyst

 Secondary Research Research Services Analyst Information Research Analyst Research Librarian / Information Specialist Knowledge & Research Analyst

Roles & Responsibilities:

Provide research support, with guidance, as part of a team serving a diverse customer base across the entire organizationConduct research using publicly available, licensed, library, legal, business, government, news, and other authoritative information sourcesPerform literature searches, environmental scans, background research, source discovery, and information synthesis in response to client requestsSummarize, synthesize, and present findings clearly in written deliverables, briefings, dashboards, alerts, newsletters, and other research products; grow towards having a perspective on direction and next steps based on the researchApproach research requests with curiosity, persistence, and sound judgment, seeking to understand the underlying business need and identify the most useful sources and outputsCommunicate effectively and responsively with customers and colleagues to build and maintain collaborative working relationships; able to evolve from order-taker to consultative research partnerApply best practices for utilizing artificial intelligence (AI) to support research activities and improve research and departmental processesCollaborate with team members to develop and maintain OS and research dashboards, alerts, and newsletters within the organization's content aggregation platformAssist department leadership with administrative activities related to vendor relationship managementManage incoming research requests through the organization's request intake platform and participate in the request management processProcess interlibrary loan requests using the OCLC Interlibrary Loan platform and distribute requested materials to customersApply knowledge of copyright and licensing restrictions when providing research materials and communicate applicable requirements to staffSolve research challenges by identifying appropriate sources, refining search strategies, evaluating source quality, and recommending practical solutionsDevelop a consultative service mindset by engaging with requestors to clarify needs, refine research questions, and provide responsive, solution-oriented support

Please note: This role centers on secondary research and the synthesis of existing information. It does not involve primary data collection, survey design, field research, laboratory research, scientific experimentation, engineering analysis, or product development research.

Basic Qualifications:

Minimum of 1 year of related research experience with a bachelor’s degree; with relevant experience who can immediately contribute at this job step; or equivalent combination of related education and work experience.Strong research and organizational skills with the ability to prioritize tasks.Intellectually curious, resourceful and persistent in pursuing answers.Proactive in clarifying research needs.Excellent verbal, written, and presentation skills; ability to communicate information to technical and non-technical professionals.Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively in a team environment, to solve problems creatively, and to effectively build partnerships.Ability and interest to grow into a consultative research partner by asking thoughtful questions, clarifying client needs, and tailoring research support accordingly.Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a Secret U.S Government issued Security Clearance. Per the U.S. Government’s eligibility requirements, you must be a U.S Citizen to be considered for a security clearance.This position requires a minimum of 3 days on-site.

Preferred Qualifications:

3 - 5 years of professional experience conducting market or federal research.Active Secret Security Clearance.Master's degree.Understanding of the federal government and the federal contracting industry.Experience in a corporate, government, or non-profit library or research environment.Familiarity with subscription databases and research tools, and appropriate use cases for them.

None

U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)

How To Apply

Connect with ORISE...on the GO! Download the new ORISE GO mobile app in the Apple App Store or Google Play Store to help you stay engaged, connected, and informed during your ORISE experience and beyond!

A Complete Application Consists Of

An applicationTranscripts – Click here for detailed information about acceptable transcriptsA current resume/CV, including academic history, employment history, relevant experiences, and publication listOne educational or professional recommendation. Your application will be considered incomplete and will not be reviewed until one recommendation is submitted.

All documents must be in English or include an official English translation.

If you have questions, send an email to ORISE.FDA.CDRH@orau.org. Please include the reference code for this opportunity in your email.

Application Deadline

12/11/2026 3:00:00 PM Eastern Time Zone

Description

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling-basis.

FDA Office and Location: A research opportunity is available within the Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH), Food and Drug Administration (FDA), located at Silver Spring, Maryland.

The mission of CDRH is to protect and promote public health. CDRH assures that patients and providers have timely and continued access to safe, effective, and high-quality medical devices and safe radiation-emitting products. CDRH provides consumers, patients, caregivers, and providers with understandable and accessible science-based information about products. CDRH facilitates medical device innovation by advancing regulatory science, providing industry with predictable, consistent, transparent, and efficient regulatory pathways, and assuring consumer confidence in devices marketed in the U.S.

Research Project: An educational research opportunity is available in the Chemical Characterization program in the FDA Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH), Office of Science and Engineering Laboratories (OSEL).

Silicone and Difficult Materials Project: This project will offer the opportunity to refine and streamline approaches to the extraction and measurement of chemicals from materials of construction that often pose exceptional difficulties during the characterization process. The data-driven methods will be developed through analysis and modeling of existing data, designing experiments, filling any deficiencies in available data, operating chromatography and mass spectrometry equipment, and participating in writing scientific articles.

Learning Objectives: Under the guidance of a mentor, you will gain experience in extractables and leachables analysis in a real-world setting as well as an understanding of regulatory science and medical device chemical characterization review processes.

Mentor: The mentor for this opportunity is Jacob Hill (jacob.hill@fda.hhs.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research, please contact the mentor.

Anticipated Appointment Start Date: June 30, 2027. Start date is flexible and will depend on a variety of factors.

Appointment Length: The appointment will initially be for one year, but may be renewed upon recommendation of FDA and is contingent on the availability of funds.

Level of Participation: The appointment is full time.

Participant Stipend: The participant will receive a monthly stipend commensurate with educational level and experience.

Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR) only.

This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education, was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and FDA. The participant will receive a monthly stipend commensurate with educational level and experience. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Participants do not become employees of FDA, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits.

Completion of a successful background investigation by the Office of Personnel Management is required for an applicant to be on-boarded at FDA. OPM can complete a background investigation only for individuals, including non-US Citizens, who have resided in the US for a total of three of the past five years.

FDA Ethics Requirements

If an ORISE Fellow, to include their spouse and minor children, reports what is identified as a Significantly Regulated Organization (SRO) or prohibited investment fund financial interest in any amount, or a relationship with an SRO, except for spousal employment with an SRO, and the individual will not voluntarily divest the financial interest or terminate the relationship, then the individual is not placed at FDA. For additional requirements, see FDA Ethics for Nonemployee Scientists.

Education

FDA requires ORISE participants to read and sign their FDA Education and Training Agreement within 30 days of his/her start date, setting forth the conditions and expectations for his/her educational appointment at the agency. This agreement covers such topics as the following:

Non-employee nature of the ORISE appointment;Prohibition on ORISE Fellows performing inherently governmental functions;Obligation of ORISE Fellows to convey all necessary rights to the FDA regarding intellectual property conceived or first reduced to practice during their fellowship;The fact that research materials and laboratory notebooks are the property of the FDA;

ORISE fellow’s obligation to protect and not to further disclose or use non-public information.

Qualifications

The qualified candidate should have received a doctoral degree in one of the relevant fields. Degree must have been received within the past five years, or anticipated to be received by December 31, 2026.

Preferred Skills

Familiarity with analytical methods such as chromatography and mass spectrometryExperience with LC-MS and GC-MS method development, optimization, and troubleshooting

Our clients turn to us when the stakes are high, the signals are difficult to interpret, and the consequences of getting it wrong are significant. We are building a new model for corporate affairs advisory and are seeking leaders who want to help define the future of the industry.

Penta’s global team brings decades of experience in business, government, communications, research, data science, and media. Our clients include many of the world's most influential organizations across technology, financial services, energy, healthcare, and other sectors, including over 25% of the Fortune 100. Penta has offices in New York, Washington DC, San Francisco, London, Brussels, Dublin, and Singapore.

$57,000 - $67,000 a year

The Role:

As an Insights and Monitoring Analyst at Penta Group, you will use research and data to help clients understand what is shaping their reputation, how their communications are performing and which emerging issues could affect their business. Working alongside experienced colleagues, you will turn your findings into clear reports, presentations and recommendations that inform advice on communications, brand, public policy and government relations.

This role is suited to a recent graduate or early career professional who follows the news, enjoys research and writing, and is interested in how companies build trust and navigate complex business and policy environments. Penta provides training and professional development to help you grow as an analyst and adviser.

Responsibilities:

Research and monitor media, social and policy developments to identify the issues, risks and narratives shaping clients’ reputations, and help prepare timely alerts and briefings. Learn clients’ businesses, audiences and goals so research addresses the questions that matter most to them. Support ongoing monitoring, benchmarking and communications measurement, as well as focused analysis on new client questions. Write clear reports and presentations that explain findings and why they matter, and contribute to recommendations. Organize and quality-check research data, including automated classifications, using Excel and research tools to spot patterns and present accurate findings Collaborate with account teams and fellow analysts and participate in client meetings. Manage deadlines, incorporate feedback and help improve the quality of our research. 

Qualifications:

A bachelor’s degree in any discipline. Communications, journalism, political science, public policy, business, history and other social sciences are all relevant. A strong interest in news, media, corporate reputation and public affairs Strong research and critical thinking skills, close attention to detail and the ability to distinguish evidence from assumption. Comfort with numbers and a working knowledge of Excel, with a willingness to build data analysis and visualization skills. Strong time management and the ability to balance multiple deadlines. A collaborative approach and a willingness to ask questions, learn from feedback and own the quality of your work. 

Salary Range:

The base salary range for this position will be $57,000 - $67,000, depending on a candidate’s experience and qualifications as they relate to the position.

rows.title: Modeling & Simulation Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Job Type

Term (Fixed Term)

Position Description

Are you passionate about using your modeling and simulation skills to address critical policy challenges? RAND is seeking talented analysts with expertise in modeling and simulation to join our team and contribute to impactful research in national security policy.

RAND analysts contribute to and lead innovative projects that deliver objective, reliable insights for the public and policymakers at multiple levels. They embrace diverse challenges on topics ranging from space vehicles to surface warfare that require strong analytic capabilities, technical knowledge, and academic or industry experience in modeling and simulation, mathematics, data science, and other applied sciences.

Why RAND?

 Reputation for Excellence: Be part of a non-profit, non-partisan organization renowned for its rigorous and objective research. Dynamic Opportunities: Collaborate in multidisciplinary teams on diverse projects that challenge and expand your skills. Poised for Impact: Your analysis will inform thousands of policymakers, clients, and other stakeholders around the world.

Responsibilities

Technical Analysts use their skills in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics to:

Develop, apply, and analyze the outputs of modeling and simulation tools to examine complex systems, assess alternatives, evaluate risks and tradeoffs, and inform decision-making.Develop understanding of national and homeland security operations and apply that knowledge to structure and design models and validate outputs.Assist in communicating the results of these analyses to decision-makers through written products, briefings, visualizations, and other media.

Term

This position is a 3-year term position with the possibility of renewal.

Qualifications

Expertise in one or more of the listed methodological areas AND one or more of the domain areas is highly desired:

Methodological AreasModeling, simulation, and analysis of complex systems, especially using the Advanced Framework for Simulation and Modeling (AFSIM)Programming and model development using Python, R, MATLAB, Julia, C++, Java, or similar languages and toolsAgent-based, discrete-event, Monte Carlo, system-dynamics, or other computational modeling approaches

Domain Areas:Space systems, aerospace systems, autonomous systems, or other defense-related technical domainsLogistics, supply chains, readiness, force planning, transportation, or operational analysisSystems engineering, requirements analysis, test and evaluation, or technology assessmentData visualization, dashboard development, or communication of complex analytic findings
All analyst positions at RAND require excellent analytic skills; the ability to communicate clearly and effectively in English, both orally and in writing; the ability to work effectively as a member of a multi-disciplinary team; and a strong commitment to RAND's core values of quality and objectivity. Experience with components of the Department of War is highly desired.

Successful applicants will demonstrate experience or strong potential in modeling and simulation, including the development, use, validation, and interpretation of models to address complex technical, operational, or policy problems.

Education Requirements

A master’s degree (or bachelor’s degree with at least five years of relevant professional analytic experience) in engineering, operations research, applied mathematics, physical sciences, computer science, data science, or related field is required. With a master's degree, at least two years relevant professional experience is preferred. This experience should demonstrate the applicant’s ability to develop, apply, analyze, or communicate the results of quantitative models, simulations, data analyses, or other analytically rigorous research products.

Security Clearance

Candidates must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance. Please note that U.S. citizenship is required to obtain and maintain a government security clearance. Candidates with an active U.S. security clearance are preferred.

Location

Washington, DC; Santa Monica, CA; Pittsburgh PA

Writing Sample Required

Successful applications will include documentation in the application package of academic and professional activities that meet stated qualifications. A writing sample is required for this position. This sample can use a recent, previously written paper or report (e.g., journal article, master’s thesis, or paper written for coursework, prior employment, or internship). Applicants with fields of study or work experience in which they have not produced written products (e.g., model development), or in which written products have dissemination restrictions, may submit a short written summary (i.e., less than one page) of one or more recent products they have developed. Applicants are encouraged to describe their specific role, the analytic or modeling methods used, and the product’s purpose or impact, as appropriate

Salary Range: $72,300 - $146,900

Overview

Systems Planning and Analysis, Inc. (SPA) delivers high-impact, technical solutions to complex national security issues. With over 50 years of business expertise and consistent growth, we are known for continuous innovation for our government customers, in both the US and abroad. Our exceptionally talented team is highly collaborative in spirit and practice, producing Results that Matter. Come work with the best! We offer opportunity, unique challenges, and clear-sighted commitment to the mission. SPA: Objective. Responsive. Trusted.

The Joint, Office of the Secretary of Defense, Interagency Division provides expert support services to a range of customers spanning across the Department of Defense, Federal Civilian, and international markets. JOID provides a diverse portfolio of analytical and programmatic capabilities to help our customers make informed decisions on their most challenging issues.

The Industry and Security Analysis Group (ISAG) within JOID provides analytical, technical, and program support to promote, grow, and protect the U.S. industrial base. ISAG’s support spans the Department of Defense (DOD), Department of Commerce, and other agencies to deliver critical decision support to national security leaders. Our team informs policy decisions, enables execution of comprehensive strategies and monitors and reports on the effectiveness of implementation. This enables senior leaders to execute strategies for developing and sustaining a robust industrial base that meets our nation’s strategic resource objectives. From policy to practice, we are a team of economic and national security professionals providing innovative solutions for our Nation’s most pressing security challenges.

We have immediate need for a 1260H Analyst with data analytic skills to provide onsite support in the Pentagon or the Mark Center (Alexandria, VA).

The 1260H Analyst will support the Office of the Deputy Assistant Secretary of War for Industrial and Investment Security (I2S) to minimize national security risk and ensure the health, resilience, and security of the DIB, as well as U.S. leadership in critical technologies. The candidate will perform open-source research, classified research, and analyze government and company-furnished information to draft due diligence products on business entities identified as possible Chinese military companies operating in the U.S., as required by the 2021 NDAA Section 1260H. The candidate will execute 1260H annual reporting activities to develop and coordinate the 1260H list with DoW and interagency stakeholders for publication. The candidate will support policy, correspondence actions, and legislative matters related to inquiries from listed companies, Congress, and interagency partners. Will leverage advanced programming tool expertise to strengthen open-source research capabilities and enhance 1260H tracking systems. The candidate will ideally possess Mandarin language capability to support specific research requirements within the program.

Desired

 Experience supporting OSW, Military Intelligence, or economic analysis for industry  Proficiency reading and understanding written Chinese  Experience leveraging or designing advanced open-source research toolsets

Description

Enterprise Knowledge (EK) is hiring for a full-time Technical Analyst to join our growing Knowledge & Data Services Sector. As a Technical Analyst, you will join a team driving Enterprise AI and semantic solutions to solve complex data challenges. In this role, you will develop frameworks to organize and unify information, leveraging inference to analyze large-scale data, answer practical business questions, and uncover unexpected connections across various industries.

As an EKer, you will join a fast-growing company that is committed to equity and inclusion, have the opportunity to work in a collaborative workplace, take advantage of our unique benefits, and help build our innovative culture. As a federal contractor, Enterprise Knowledge will not sponsor a new applicant for employment authorization or offer any immigration related support for this position (i.e., H1B, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, F-1 CPT, J-1, TN, E-2, E-3, L-1, and O-1, or any EADs or other forms of work authorization that require immigration support from an employer.

1 to 3 years of experience working in project-based work and/or client-facing roles Bachelor’s degree in a field with strong emphasis in business or data analysis, information systems, philosophy, or other fields related to technology and analysisProven leadership skills demonstrating strong judgment, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities as well as working collaboratively as part of a teamExcellent organizational skills and attention to detail coupled with the ability to multitaskExceptional communication skills (verbal, written, and visual) with experience in presentations and/or facilitationDetail-oriented to be "last eye" on deliverables The ability to meet daily, weekly, and long-term deadlines in a fast-paced environmentThe ability to work independently and proactively on various projects with minimal supervisionAbility to engage professionally with a diverse range of stakeholders including executives, managers, and subject matter expertsAptitude to quickly learn new skills and abilities on-the-job

Salary Information

The salary range for this role is $88,000 to $93,000, with most candidates likely to fall in the lower half. This range does not guarantee a specific salary and may be adjusted based on the needs of the company and the candidate’s qualifications.

Data Privacy Notice

Enterprise Knowledge (EK) is committed to protecting your personal information. When you submit your application, we collect and process your personal data solely for recruitment and hiring purposes. We will not use your information for any other purpose without your explicit consent.

Requests for such changes will be reviewed and accommodated unless the burden or expense of providing access would be disproportionate to the risks to your privacy, or where the rights of other individuals may be affected.

By submitting your application, you acknowledge that you have read and understood this notice. If you have any questions about how we handle your personal data or need to update your information, please contact us at careers@enterprise-knowledge.com.

rows.descriptionText:
Data is at the center of everything we do. As a startup, we disrupted the credit card industry by individually personalizing every credit card offer using statistical modeling and the relational database, cutting edge technology in 1988! Fast-forward a few years, and this little innovation and our passion for data has skyrocketed us to a Fortune 200 company and a leader in the world of data-driven decision-making.

As a Data Scientist at Capital One, you’ll be part of a team that’s leading the next wave of disruption at a whole new scale, using the latest in computing and machine learning technologies and operating across billions of customer records to unlock the big opportunities that help everyday people save money, time and agony in their financial lives.

Team Description

Join the creditflow team, the engine powering our next-generation credit decisioning and valuations model scoring platform. Our mission is to seamlessly connect complex financial data with real-time analytics to optimize credit polity, enhance cash flow underwriting, and deliver lightning-fast credit decisions via valuations model and various analytical capabilities.

As a Senior Data Scientist on the team, you will build a robust scoring platform and deploy models, create innovative analytical tools, leverage alternative data sources, and collaborate cross-functionally with engineering and product to scale our products, valuations models and analytical capabilities. We operate in a highly collaborative, fast-paced environment where your expertise in data, engineering, business and credit knowledge along with machine learning and statistical modeling—powered by a tech stack featuring Python, Snowflake, Conda—will directly impact our credit infrastructure and empower our customers with fairer, more accessible credit products.

Role Description

In this role, you will:

Partner with a cross-functional team of data scientists, software engineers, and product managers to deliver a product customers loveLeverage a broad stack of technologies — Python, Conda, AWS, H2O, Spark, and more — to reveal the insights hidden within huge volumes of numeric and textual dataBuild machine learning models through all phases of development, from design through training, evaluation, validation, and implementationFlex your interpersonal skills to translate the complexity of your work into tangible business goals

The Ideal Candidate is:

Innovative. You continually research and evaluate emerging technologies. You stay current on published state-of-the-art methods, technologies, and applications and seek out opportunities to apply them. Creative. You thrive on bringing definition to big, undefined problems. You love asking questions and pushing hard to find answers. You’re not afraid to share a new idea. Technical. You’re comfortable with open-source languages and are passionate about developing further. You have hands-on experience developing data science solutions using open-source tools and cloud computing platforms. Statistically-minded. You’ve built models, validated them, and backtested them. You know how to interpret a confusion matrix or a ROC curve. You have experience with clustering, classification, sentiment analysis, time series, and deep learning. A data guru. “Big data” doesn’t faze you. You have the skills to retrieve, combine, and analyze data from a variety of sources and structures. You know understanding the data is often the key to great data science. 

Basic Qualifications:

Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining one of the following with an expectation that the required degree will be obtained on or before the scheduled start date:A Bachelor's Degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) plus 2 years of experience performing data analyticsA Master's Degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) or an MBA with a quantitative concentration
Preferred Qualifications:

Master’s Degree in “STEM” field (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics), or PhD in “STEM” field (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics)Experience working with AWSAt least 2 years’ experience in Python, Scala, or RAt least 2 years’ experience with machine learningAt least 2 years’ experience with SQL

rows.descriptionText:
Data is at the center of everything we do. As a startup, we disrupted the credit card industry by individually personalizing every credit card offer using statistical modeling and the relational database, cutting edge technology in 1988! Fast-forward a few years, and this little innovation and our passion for data has skyrocketed us to a Fortune 200 company and a leader in the world of data-driven decision-making.

As a Data Scientist at Capital One, you’ll be part of a team that’s leading the next wave of disruption at a whole new scale, using the latest in computing and machine learning technologies and operating across billions of customer records to unlock the big opportunities that help everyday people save money, time and agony in their financial lives.

Team Description:

The Credit Risk Management, Loss Forecasting and Allowance team uses the latest technologies and innovative models and data to forecast and optimize future losses associated with Capital One’s credit card portfolio. We partner with model development and software engineering teams to build predictive models and automate insight generation.

As a Data Scientist, you will focus on loss forecasting modernization and data transformation. The qualified candidate will support card loss forecasting: resilience, outlook, allowance and CCAR.

Partner with a cross-functional team of data scientists, software engineers, and product managers to identify and quantify risks associated with modelsLeverage a broad stack of technologies — Python, Conda, AWS, Spark, and more — to reveal the insights hidden within dataBuild statistical/machine learning models to challenge “champion models” that are deployed in production todayContribute to the model governance of the next generation of machine learning modelsFlex your interpersonal skills to present how model risks could impact the business to executives 

The Ideal Candidate is:

Innovative. You continually research and evaluate emerging technologies. You stay current on published state-of-the-art methods, technologies, and applications and seek out opportunities to apply them. Creative. You thrive on bringing definition to big, undefined problems. You love asking questions and pushing hard to find answers. You’re not afraid to share a new idea. Technical. You’re comfortable with open-source languages and are passionate about developing further. You have hands-on experience developing data science solutions using open-source tools and cloud computing platforms. Statistically-minded. You’ve built models, validated them, and backtested them. You have experience with a wide array of methods. A data guru. “Big data” doesn’t faze you. You have the skills to retrieve, combine, and analyze data from a variety of sources and structures. You know understanding the data is often the key to great data science.

Purpose and Impact:

Amentum provides warning and all-source analytical support to DIA’s Defense Combating Terrorism Office to drive DoD policy, planning, and operational decisions to counter regional and transnational terrorism threats. We conduct mission-critical counterterrorism analysis focused on operational and strategic effects against emerging terrorist threat networks and identities operating globally with intent to harm U.S. persons, facilities, and interests. Our work includes delivering national watchlisting support to the TIDE database, providing expert assessments for the Pentagon/Joint Staff, and 24/7/365 support to DoD and senior policy decision makers, as well as international and interagency partners, on predictive threat assessments regarding transnational and regional terrorist threats. Amentum analysts also support the Congressionally-mandated Prisoner of War/Missing in Action cell with analysis, collection, and 24/7 support to the U.S. government for global hostage threats or events against U.S. citizens.

Work Schedule: First Shift – 8 hours per day

Essential Responsibilities:

Systematically and deliberately reviews DoD datasets assessed as likely to contain identifying information for known or suspected terrorists. Identity, prioritize, and record information from known DoD datasets related to known or suspected terrorists as specified by the Government. Crosscheck/research known or suspected terrorists against other intelligence holdings to ensure completeness of information and to avoid duplicating data entries. Compile information into a nomination report format as specified by the Government. Correctly format, classify, and address reports. Ensure information contained within reports is intelligible, cogent, comprehensive, and understandable, and that all reports use proper grammar and spelling. Meet Terrorist Identity Nomination (TIN) production schedule. Correct and resubmit incorrect reports and prepare reports for dissemination as record message traffic or other dissemination methods as specified by the Government. Provide guidance and instruction for less experienced team members assigned to Watchlisting. Demonstrate general knowledge and understanding of IC organizations associated with CT operations, analysis, products, and information systems. Attend and participate in meetings, conferences, intelligence exchanges, roundtables, working groups, and other types of analytic exchanges in support or DIA’s Watchlisting mission. Possess general information systems experience working with select DoD datasets and intelligence reporting activities: demonstrate comprehensive mission knowledge in order to provide guidance related to National Terrorist Watchlisting policies and procedures. Demonstrate in-depth knowledge and understanding of terrorist organizations, to include group names and geographic location, leadership, activities, and ideology. 

Minimum Requirements (Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities):

Watchlist Analyst – Performs all-source intelligence analysis of DoD datasets to identify and nominate known or suspected terrorists into the National Terrorist Watchlisting system. Develops DoD recommendations for the no-fly, selectee, or other national terrorist watch lists as appropriate, to fulfill the DoD component of Homeland Security Presidential Directives (HSPDs) 6 and 11 and reviews DoD datasets for identifying information of Known or Suspected Terrorists; and identifies, prioritizes, and records information from DoD datasets as specified by the Government. Produces analytic reports using DIA’s Watchlisting Data Organizer (WATCHDOG) and / or other internal DIA production tools. Prepares reports for dissemination by methods specified by the Government.

Description

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling-basis.

FDA Office and Location: A research opportunity is available at the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER) Office of Rare Diseases, Pediatrics, Urologic and Reproductive Medicine (ORPURM), in the Division of Pediatrics and Maternal Health (DPMH) located in Silver Spring, Maryland. The participation is hybrid with some in-person at the FDA White Oak Campus in Silver Spring, Maryland.

The Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER) performs an essential public health task by making sure that safe and effective drugs are available to improve the health of people in the United States. As part of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), CDER regulates over-the-counter and prescription drugs, including biological therapeutics and generic drugs. These efforts cover more than just medicines.

Research Project: Pediatric extrapolation relies on the use of inferences about efficacy in children often based on data in adults based on assumptions or evidence of similarity in disease, drug pharmacology and treatment response between adults and children. The need to systematically assess the assumptions underlying extrapolation is well recognized in pediatric drug development. The FDA has access to data from approximately 1,200 pediatric clinical trials, including data from 600 trials spanning more than 300 pediatric development programs, which enables a systematic, disease-focused review. The proposed project aims to analyze adult and pediatric clinical trial data to evaluate the assumptions underlying the extrapolation of pharmacokinetics (PK), efficacy, and safety for selected diseases/conditions.

Educational and Training Components: You will participate in activities related to the research project, including data collection from public and proprietary sources, data analysis and interpretation, and preparation and presentation of research findings for scientific dissemination and publication.

Learning Objectives: Under the guidance of the mentor(s), you will be involved in a systematic review of adult and pediatric clinical trial data, assess similarities of disease between adults and children; understand expected treatment response differences in children, if any; you will assess possibility of leveraging information from previous studies (adult and pediatric) and provide a framework for optimizing trials.

Mentor: The mentor for this opportunity is Lily (Yeruk) Mulugeta (yeruk.mulugeta@fda.hhs.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research, please contact the mentor.

Anticipated Appointment Start Date: January 2027. Start date is flexible and will depend on a variety of factors.

Appointment Length: The appointment will initially be for one year, but may be renewed upon recommendation of FDA and is contingent on the availability of funds.

Level of Participation: The participation is hybrid with some in-person at the FDA White Oak Campus in Silver Spring, Maryland.

Participant Stipend: The participant will receive a monthly stipend commensurate with educational level and experience.

Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR) only.

This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education, was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and FDA. The participant will receive a monthly stipend commensurate with educational level and experience. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Participants do not become employees of FDA, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits.

Completion of a successful background investigation by the Office of Personnel Management is required for an applicant to be on-boarded at FDA. OPM can complete a background investigation only for individuals, including non-US Citizens, who have resided in the US for a total of three of the past five years.

rows.title: Research Associate
rows.descriptionText:
At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future.

Department Summary:

The Market Intelligence and Research team

MITRE is seeking a curious and collaborative early career Research Analyst, Research Associate, Information Professional, or Librarian to join our Research Services team, a part of MITRE’s Market Intelligence & Research organization. This individual will be responsible for providing, locating, gathering, and analyzing information from third-parties, open-source news and articles, published research papers, subscription and public databases and other sources in support of MITRE’s work programs, and specific sponsor and MITRE initiatives.

As a research associate, this key team member will need a growing understanding and/or interest in databases, digital research libraries, query techniques and short cuts, research and information management practices, and OS intelligence platforms (news alerts, dashboards). This role focuses on desk research, secondary research, literature searching/review, open-source and subscription-based research, and synthesis of existing information for internal clients. This is not a primary research, laboratory, engineering, scientific, or product research role.

This role will translate internal client questions into tangible research objectives to meet the needs of our customers and will engage with internal clients to scope and prioritize tasks, collecting and working with a variety of research outputs, and performing additional desk and secondary research as necessary. This position supports other department capabilities in business analyses, strategy, and sponsor and market intelligence as needed. This role will interact with all levels of the company, including senior level managers, technical SMEs, and analysts.

The ideal candidate is intellectually curious, highly motivated to find answers, and eager to develop a consultative approach to research support by helping clients refine questions, identify the most relevant sources, and shape actionable outputs. The ideal candidate will have interest in performing research on a broad range of topics, an entrepreneurial approach to generating and creating value and impact, and an appreciation for a nonprofit/public interest environment.

Research Analyst

 Secondary Research Research Services Analyst Information Research Analyst Research Librarian / Information Specialist Knowledge & Research Analyst

Roles & Responsibilities:

Provide research support, with guidance, as part of a team serving a diverse customer base across the entire organizationConduct research using publicly available, licensed, library, legal, business, government, news, and other authoritative information sourcesPerform literature searches, environmental scans, background research, source discovery, and information synthesis in response to client requestsSummarize, synthesize, and present findings clearly in written deliverables, briefings, dashboards, alerts, newsletters, and other research products; grow towards having a perspective on direction and next steps based on the researchApproach research requests with curiosity, persistence, and sound judgment, seeking to understand the underlying business need and identify the most useful sources and outputsCommunicate effectively and responsively with customers and colleagues to build and maintain collaborative working relationships; able to evolve from order-taker to consultative research partnerApply best practices for utilizing artificial intelligence (AI) to support research activities and improve research and departmental processesCollaborate with team members to develop and maintain OS and research dashboards, alerts, and newsletters within the organization's content aggregation platformAssist department leadership with administrative activities related to vendor relationship managementManage incoming research requests through the organization's request intake platform and participate in the request management processProcess interlibrary loan requests using the OCLC Interlibrary Loan platform and distribute requested materials to customersApply knowledge of copyright and licensing restrictions when providing research materials and communicate applicable requirements to staffSolve research challenges by identifying appropriate sources, refining search strategies, evaluating source quality, and recommending practical solutionsDevelop a consultative service mindset by engaging with requestors to clarify needs, refine research questions, and provide responsive, solution-oriented support

Please note: This role centers on secondary research and the synthesis of existing information. It does not involve primary data collection, survey design, field research, laboratory research, scientific experimentation, engineering analysis, or product development research.

Basic Qualifications:

Minimum of 1 year of related research experience with a bachelor’s degree; with relevant experience who can immediately contribute at this job step; or equivalent combination of related education and work experience.Strong research and organizational skills with the ability to prioritize tasks.Intellectually curious, resourceful and persistent in pursuing answers.Proactive in clarifying research needs.Excellent verbal, written, and presentation skills; ability to communicate information to technical and non-technical professionals.Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively in a team environment, to solve problems creatively, and to effectively build partnerships.Ability and interest to grow into a consultative research partner by asking thoughtful questions, clarifying client needs, and tailoring research support accordingly.Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a Secret U.S Government issued Security Clearance. Per the U.S. Government’s eligibility requirements, you must be a U.S Citizen to be considered for a security clearance.This position requires a minimum of 3 days on-site.

Preferred Qualifications:

3 - 5 years of professional experience conducting market or federal research.Active Secret Security Clearance.Master's degree.Understanding of the federal government and the federal contracting industry.Experience in a corporate, government, or non-profit library or research environment.Familiarity with subscription databases and research tools, and appropriate use cases for them.

None

None

$62,500 - $78,000 - $93,500 Annual

Onsite
